I know I recommended against new development, but wanted to show you just in case.

* New building: $2,373 is the first-year figure. Taxes are projected to rise about 50% once the building is fully assessed, which would bring the monthly to about $3,040. Common charges in small buildings like this (16 apartments) can also jump: in my study of 44 small Upper East Side condos, 12 had a one-year jump of more than 10% and 6 of more than 20%, and the budget here is thin ($1,500 a year for repairs and $7,000 for reserves). If common charges jumped 50% on top of the tax increase, the monthly would be about $3,700 within three years. Listed at $2.25M (the offering plan price was $2.0M). There is likely to be a part-time doorman, 9 to 5 on weekdays. Closings begin in early 2027. Pied-à-terre tax: the city value of this apartment should be well under the $1M line, so the surcharge is not expected to apply.

I know I recommended against new development, but wanted to show you just in case.

Said to be taxed at full value already, but common charges in small buildings like this can jump. In my study of 44 small Upper East Side condos, 12 had a one-year jump of more than 10% and 6 of more than 20%; several rose 50–60% (1165 Madison +54%, 320 East 82nd +52%). A 50% jump here would take common charges from $2,019 to about $3,030 a month. If that happened within three years, the monthly would be about $6,000. Pied-à-terre tax: the city values this apartment at $1.02M, just over the $1M line, so a 4% surcharge will apply unless it is Olalla and Daniel's legal primary residence. That could be up to about $40,000 a year in extra taxes.
